newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- GRID'S PLEA ON WINDFALL TAX

National Grid is pressing Labour to exclude the company from the proposed windfall tax on privatised utilities, arguing that the 50 sterling rebate handed out to customers after financial reconstruction last summer meant it had already paid out on a windfall. Grid yesterday confirmed that job cuts would be larger than expected after the recent price review.
-- DELAY FOR BA ON US ALLIANCE PLAN

Attempts by British Airways to speed up the government decision-making process on its proposed alliance with American Airlines face further delays. Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang has asked director general of Fair Trading John Bridgeman whether he has any further reservations about the deal.
-- CHANNEL OPERATORS' FERRY MERRY XMAS

Cross-Channel ferry operators P&O and Stena have benefited from the Channel Tunnel fire to the tune of 50 per cent traffic increases on the Dover-Calais route, despite the French lorry blockade at Calais. P&O has an interavailability agreement with Eurotunnel, under which it carries Eurotunnel passengers.
THE TIMES
-- BUDGET GIVEN CAUTIOUS WELCOME BY BUSINESS

Kenneth Clarke's Budget has been welcomed by business leaders as prudent and ignoring the pressure for pre-election expansion measures, instead going for moves to cut public borrowing and sustain overall economic growth. They were a little more skeptical about a 1p cut in income tax and its effect on inflation and maintained a general belief that interest rates are likely to go up again before the general election.
-- ANGLO GIVES EU PLATINUM ASSURANCE

The South African mining group, Anglo American, said yesterday it is hopeful of striking an agreement with the European Commission over its stake in Lonrho, the hotels to platinum group. The Commission is alarmed by the prospect of a single player dominating the platinum market. Anglo reported headline earnings for six months to September 30 of 310 million sterling, up 22 per cent.
-- EUROTUNNEL DEBT DEAL DELAYED

Due to the fire in the Channel tunnel last week, Eurotunnel is being forced to put new clauses into its 9 billion stg debt restructuring agreement. Senior bankers believe this move will cause a delay of possibly months before a deal, which has been agreed in outline last month, can be put to the 225-strong banking syndicate for ratification.
THE GUARDIAN
-- OIL FIRMS FACE 13 BILLION POUND CLEAN-UP BILL

The key finding of a confidential report commissioned for the European Union's environment and energy directives is that Europe's oil and gas companies face a 13.6 billion sterling bill for disposing of offshore rigs and platforms. The report details fears about the fate of over 1,600 offshore installations.
-- SEVERN TRENT TO BUY BACK SHARES

Severn Trent, the privatised water group, is poised to go ahead with proposals to buy back as much as 10 per cent of its shares. The move would cost the U.K.'s largest privatised water group, close to 274 million sterling. Yesterday, the board, stated that it would start buying back shares as soon as is appropriate. The buy-back won approval at the last annual meeting.
-- PORTILLO LIFTS HOPES OF GERMAN ORDER FOR EUROFIGHTER

Hopes were raised yesterday for the safeguarding of up to 100,000 British jobs after Michael Portillo, the Defence Secretary, said he was pretty confident about Germany's commitment to the four-nation Eurofighter project. British Aerospace will build the aircraft at its sites in Lancashire and Humberside and the engines will be provided by Rolls-Royce's Bristol plant.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- AT&T DROPS ENERGIS ACQUISITION FROM EXPANSION PLANS

AT&T's U.K. expansion plans were put into confusion yesterday when it emerged that it had abandoned talks to buy Energis, the long- distance telephones company owned by the National Grid. The Grid has confirmed that it is in talks with a handful of companies about an alliance with Energis, which would most likely involve the outside firm taking a 50 per cent stake int he venture.
-- UBS MAY BE DEMOTED FROM BANKING ELITE

Union Bank of Switzerland announced yesterday 3 billion Swiss Francs of provisions driving it to an estimated and record 0.5 billion Swiss Francs loss for the year. The news could send UBS from the elite club of "Triple A" credit rated banks. The provisions are for potential bad debts in the bank's domestic lending operations and do not take account of a separate announcement of a consolidation of its 31 economic areas into eight resulting in 800 redundancies.
-- PEARSON SNAPS UP US PUBLISHER FOR 200 MILLION POUNDS

Pearson announced yesterday the acquisition of Putnam Berkley, the US publishing house, from MCA, the giant entertainment group, for 200 million pounds stg. The deal, made through Pearson's Penguin Books subsidiary, will make Penguin the second largest publisher in the world.
